About us
OpenText is a leading Cloud and AI company that provides organizations around the world with a comprehensive suite of Business AI, Business Clouds, and Business Technology. We help organizations grow, innovate, become more efficient and effective, and do so in a trusted and secure way—through Information Management.

OpenText (NASDAQ/TSX: OTEX), founded in 1991 in Waterloo, has a rich history of helping customers manage their most important asset—information. Originating from a collaboration to digitize the Oxford English Dictionary, OpenText has grown into a global leader in information management. With over 120,000 enterprise customers across 180 countries, OpenText supports 98 of the top 100 global companies. A wide breadth of offerings uniquely positions OpenText to help customers unlock the value of that information using Al, cloud, and security innovations.

At OpenText, our culture is at the heart of everything we do—and today, that includes being proudly AI-first. We’re creating a workplace where everyone can thrive, with artificial intelligence integrated into how we work, solve problems, and innovate together.

By fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment, we empower digital knowledge workers and drive forward-thinking solutions that shape the future of information management. We believe our success comes from the strength of our team—talent that AI can’t replace—and we’re committed to attracting and supporting those who bring unique insight, adaptability, and creativity.
Because at OpenText, people aren’t just our greatest asset—they’re the reason we shine in an AI-powered world. Join us at OpenText and become part of a team where your talents and ideas are truly valued.

Would you bet your job on your company's AI agents?

At
OpenText
World 2026, I heard a fascinating story. Almost every executive had an AI pilot. But when asked if they would bet their job on its success, most hands went down.

That says a lot about where we are with AI today.

I spent the day talking with executives, meeting the teams behind the technology, and testing AI agents myself.

What I discovered surprised me. From a hospital turning a 12 month project into 8 weeks, to a company deliberately limiting its AI autonomy, even when it could do more.

The biggest lesson? The future of AI isn't just about what agents can do. It's about what we can trust them to do.

Curious to hear which story surprises you most. 👇

What does an Oreo cookie have to do with the future of AI?
More than you might think!

At
OpenText
World, CEO
Ayman Antoun
used an Oreo to explain a fundamental challenge with enterprise AI.

Imagine a supermarket in Austin. It's back to school season, Oreos are on promotion, and the shelves are suddenly empty.

The store places an urgent order.

But an order number is just a bunch of digits.

To fulfill it, an AI agent needs to connect that order to the right store, identify which warehouse has available stock, and understand when and where the delivery must happen.

Data tells the agent WHAT happened. Connected data and trusted context tell it WHAT TO DO about it.

That's how an order number becomes a fulfilled delivery.

And there's a reason OpenText chose this example.
Mondelēz International
, the maker of Oreos, is one of its customers.

OpenText's ambition is precisely this: to turn fragmented enterprise data into trusted context that AI agents can use to make better decisions and take action.

It made me reflect on something bigger.

We're spending billions making AI models smarter. But intelligence without business context can simply produce wrong decisions faster.

I am convinced that the next breakthrough in enterprise AI will not be a smarter model. It will be giving AI a better understanding of how our businesses actually work.

What do you think? Are we focusing too much on AI intelligence and not enough on the context it needs?

In partnership with OpenText.
